item.title: Beppu Aquarium (Umitamago) — Guide
item.description: Beppu is home to a popular seaside aquarium on the shore of Beppu Bay (widely known as Umitamago, the ‘sea egg’), making a fun, family-friendly outing and a welcome change of pace from the town’s hot springs. The aquarium presents a wide variety of marine life across its tanks and exhibits — from a large main tank and colourful reef fish to seals, otters, and playful star performers like walruses and dolphins.

item.title: Beppu Mud Onsen (Doroyu) — Guide
item.description: Beppu’s mud onsen (doroyu) is a rare and prized type of hot spring where you bathe not in clear water but in warm, naturally occurring mineral mud. Found in the Myoban and Kannawa areas, these springs produce a soft, silky, greyish clay mud, rich in minerals, that you can smooth over your skin and soak in. Bathing in the warm mud is deeply relaxing and, thanks to its mineral content, is traditionally believed to soften, cleanse and beautify the skin, leaving it smooth afterwards.

item.title: Beppu Onsen Day Trip from Miyazaki — Guide
item.description: While Beppu lies just over the border in Oita prefecture, its fame as Japan’s greatest onsen town makes it a popular addition to a wider Kyushu itinerary that includes Miyazaki. Set on a bay ringed by volcanic mountains, Beppu produces a colossal volume of hot-spring water across eight districts, with columns of white steam constantly rising over the town. Its signature attraction is the ‘Hells of Beppu’ — a tour of vividly coloured hot springs, from a cobalt-blue pool to a blood-red pond, that are for viewing rather than bathing — alongside an incredible variety of baths to soak in: sand baths, mud baths, steam baths and countless open-air rotenburo.

item.title: Beppu Onsen Festival — Guide
item.description: The Beppu Onsen Festival (Beppu Onsen Matsuri), held each year in early April, is the town’s biggest celebration, giving thanks to the gods and the earth for the endless bounty of hot springs that has made Beppu Japan’s greatest onsen town. Over several days the whole town comes alive with festivities: colourful parades with music, dance and floats through the streets, a lively hot-spring ‘mikoshi’ (portable shrine), and events across Beppu’s eight hot-spring districts.

item.title: Beppu Sand Bath (Sunamushi) — Guide
item.description: The sand bath (sunamushi onsen) is one of Beppu’s most distinctive and enjoyable hot-spring experiences. Wearing a light cotton yukata, you lie down and attendants shovel warm, damp volcanic sand — heated naturally from below by the hot springs — over your body until you are buried up to the neck. As you lie cocooned in the heavy, gently steaming sand, the warmth penetrates deeply and evenly, promoting circulation and inducing a profound, drowsy relaxation quite different from a normal soak, often described as detoxifying.

item.title: Kannawa Onsen Town — Guide
item.description: Kannawa is the most atmospheric of Beppu’s eight hot-spring areas and one of the most evocative onsen townscapes in Japan. Here the geothermal power is so intense that clouds of white steam constantly billow up from vents, drains and rooftops all over the hillside district, drifting between the old wooden inns, narrow lanes and shops and wrapping the whole town in a dreamlike, primeval haze. Strolling the steaming streets — a walk sometimes called the ‘yukemuri’ (steam) experience — is a magical, only-in-Beppu pleasure, especially atmospheric in the cool of morning or evening when the steam is thickest.
